name: Module 5: capsule release and library cleanup
description: Steps 16 and 17. Opens the capsule shells, recovers the DNA, captures it on magnetic beads, washes and elutes a finished library. 30 x 20 mm, 0.3 mm deep, hot-embossed COC. RELEASE IS A MATRIX-DIGESTING ENZYME AT 37 C, NOT A BROAD-SPECTRUM PROTEASE. Published work shows a broad-spectrum protease leaves a crosslinked capsule intact and still holding its DNA, while a matrix-digesting enzyme digests the gelatin backbone between crosslinks until the network dissolves; a divalent-cation chelator inhibits the matrix-digesting enzyme, so it must be absent from the incoming buffer. react_cx is that digest, and it needs only 37 C, which is why this chip has no high-temperature requirement of its own. bead_cx is an open capture chamber over an external magnet with a 0.5 mm floor so the field reaches the beads. THERE IS NO MECHANICAL BEAD TRAP, and there cannot be: SPRI beads are about 1 um and the smallest feature either process can make is 200 um, so retention is purely magnetic and the geometry only shapes the flow. EITHER ORDER WORKS. The project protocol sheet runs index PCR before release, but published practice for these capsules is release first, then PCR. With the magnet off, react_cx drains through bead_cx to out_waste, so this chip can run before module 4 as well as after it; only the order of passes changes, not the geometry. Two honest limits are recorded in protocols/module5_design.md: the ethanol wash and dry that SPRI normally needs will smear the pellet, because a drying meniscus pulls on a bead about 100,000 times harder than the magnet, so ratio-based size selection stays in a tube for the MVP; and the dissolved shell contributes roughly 10,000 times more polymer mass than there is DNA, so the eluate must be diluted before it ever meets the beads. out_lib is the product path, kept short and narrow because the whole output is a few microlitres and DNA adsorbs to polymer. THE NARROWNESS IS IN THE CHANNEL, NOT THE BORE. ch_out_lib stays 0.3 mm wide, which is what keeps the wetted polymer area small; the PORT was also written as 300 um and that was wrong, because 300 um is below fabrication_floors.min_port_mm (0.8 mm) in contracts/blocks.json - we cannot drill or print a reliable 300 um through-hole and no fitting mates to one, so the product would have had no way off the chip at all. out_lib is now 800 um, the floor exactly, which costs a fraction of a microlitre of extra bore volume and buys a port that exists. Re-checked after widening: the nearest port is out_waste at 11.00 mm centre to centre (floor 5 mm), every other pair is further, the 0.4 mm bore wall to the 30 x 20 mm edge is 1.60 mm in x and 2.60 mm in y, and the bore clears every chamber and every channel it is not connected to. out_lib stays capsule_passable false and must: what leaves here is eluted library DNA in solution, the shells are already dissolved in react_cx and the ~1 um beads are held magnetically in bead_cx, so nothing particulate is meant to reach it - and 800 um would pass a 70 um capsule, so the flag records intent rather than a size limit. Geometry is ours; the chemistry is cited in protocols/module5_v1.json.

ports.note: Product outlet. 800 um is fabrication_floors.min_port_mm exactly: the 300 um bore this once declared is undrillable and unconnectable, so it was widened. The narrow part of the product path is ch_out_lib (0.3 mm), not the bore. capsule_passable stays false because only eluted DNA in solution leaves here - the shells are dissolved and the beads are held magnetically in bead_cx.
